The ending feels completely natural and earned because it reaches the exact thematic and emotional climax the narrative has been building toward. Throughout the story, the narrator is mysteriously drawn to the burned chair and the couple, admitting he is "in the mood for ruins" and looking for something he can't quite name. The climax occurs when he watches the woman reclaim and sit in her ruined chair amidst the flood, prompting his realization that he has spent his life walking away from his own "ruined things" (specifically the letters he burned years ago) rather than facing or reclaiming them. The final scene, where he returns to his own flooded home and sits on the bare floor because he has nothing left of his past to sit in, brings the central motifs of fire, water, and the chair full circle, providing a deeply resonant and purposeful sense of closure.
